blocks.passage: Small acts of kindness such as giving someone a gift, giving your seat on public transportation to someone who needs it, giving a smile to a stranger, or offering someone to carry something for them can make a big difference in your life. They do not take much time, but they do require thoughtfulness and effort. A simple kind phrase like "you look great today!", a heartfelt thank you or, a friendly word can make someone's day. It can make them smile and feel good. This is the "power of kindness". Such small acts of kindness are the basis of many successful relationships.

blocks.passage: Water is the most essential element in our life. We cannot think of life without water. We need it to drink, wash our bodies and clothes, cook our food and grow crops, vegetables and fruits. Water is also essential for animals, birds, insects, etc. We need huge resources of it to produce electricity on a large and commercial scale. Nearly 70 percent of our body is water. No living being can exist for long without water, the most valuable liquid. We use oceans, seas, rivers and lakes as waterways to carry goods, passengers, etc. Lack of water causes a lot of problems for us, so saving it is necessary. For example, using a dishwasher saves much more water than hand washing. In short, water is very important to our life and our planet.

blocks.passage:
One of the most essential issues which nations must consider these days is providing energy for their people. In the past, energy was produced from fossil fuels such as oil, coal, and natural gas. Although such fuels have been main resources for years, they are harmful to the environment. They have caused serious problems including air or water pollution, global warming and health problems. Also, they take millions of years to form, so they are nonrenewable — cannot be replaced easily.
To reduce bad effects of nonrenewable energy, scientists are trying to replace it with other energy resources which are friendly to the environment. Such energy sources are called clean energy as they reduce the environmental risks and don't cause serious problems for humans. They are made from resources that can be replaced like wind, water, sunshine, tides and plants. As a vast country that is rich in sun radiation during most time of the year, Iran can generate enough energy by setting solar panels in desert areas like Yazd, south of Semnan or Kashan. In short, it seems that replacing fossil fuels with solar energy is the main solution to the various problems caused by burning fossil fuels.
